original_card.question: Can one exact all-size/compiler, precision, hosting or restoration implication be proved or falsified?
methods: Prove one missing implication with explicit quantified hypotheses.
Find an exact counterexample at the claimed interface boundary.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Identify the proposition and what would change downstream; do not equate a finite replay with a universal proof.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected review scope and choose one exact all-size or precision implication.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Write its quantified inputs and conclusion; find a missing hypothesis or construct a minimal exact adversarial instance.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Finite supplier improvements are useful only under the retained transfer obligations.
allowed_variations: Choose one tape, precision, hosting or restoration lemma.
scope_change_triggers: Replacing a quantified obligation with another finite smoke test.

actual_scope: One hosting implication for the selected PR589 bit supplier: do the window-free partial width-seven rows of merged #1023 and merged #1281 (width-7 residuals placed in capacity-7 idle slots without time order) survive PR442's replica-local hosting windows (audit_hosted_k: s in W[i] for every hosted slot) on the frozen nine-stage recipe, whole residuals, no banks? Exact window-respecting optimum and certificate for every k = 0..74.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for one exact hosting implication. This narrows it to the time-order hypothesis that #1023 lists as unchecked, and to the per-replica, frozen-recipe part of #1281's open question 1. That question's PR1179 boundary-contract audit and cross-replica pooling stay open, as do projector compatibility, owner inactivity and a physical width-7 helper.
bottleneck_link: Side result on the bit supplier; the selected record is complex-bound, so no kappa changes. Under #1023's one-unit local pricing, the frozen recipe and replica-local hosting, it corrects the bit headroom a partial width-seven helper mechanism can buy: the window-respecting optimum keeps 63.6-67.1% (optimistic) or 56.3-60.7% (pessimistic) of the window-free gain, i.e. the published rows overstate it by about 1.5x or 1.7x, roughly flat in k.
stop_rule: Stop once every k = 0..74 has an explicit window-feasible placement and a tight grid certificate under both local brackets, k = 0 reproduces the selected bit endpoint, and every #1023 and #1281 row is compared; report any row not decided instead of claiming it.
evidence: RESULT.json: the nine-stage idle schedule equals, event by event and field by field, the global_k.py reference (its recipe() and idle-insertion block executed via ast inside a transcribed loop); three window predicates agree on it; the frozen selection lies inside. Capacity-7 children 1/3/5 admit only stages 2/4/6, so at most 3k of 9k width-7 residuals per replica sit in 7-slots. Exact window-respecting optimum, an explicit placement built and checked at run time, and a tight 1e-24 certificate for every k = 0..74, both brackets; k = 0 reproduces 0.001733427039589844234749. k = 37 optimistic 0.001770809187 (+2.157%) vs window-free 0.001789671631 (+3.245%); k = 74 0.001809907119 (+4.412%) vs 0.001849754238 (+6.711%). Retained fraction 0.636-0.671 (optimistic), 0.563-0.607 (pessimistic). All 8 #1023 partial rows unreachable; #1281's closed-form local optimum transcribed and checked against its 75 idle profiles; all 148 local rows priced here from it (8 also priced by #1281, reproduced exactly in local endpoint and histogram) lie above the per-replica bound, as do #1281's 8 priced pooled32 rows with k > 0. Chain reduction confirmed by max-flow on every distribution (462 at k = 1, 6188 at k = 2). #1023's all-width-7 optimum stays window-feasible (104 sextet splits). 14 tests pass.

open_questions.question: Can cross-replica (T16-style) interleaved owner maps lift the one-stage capacity-7 windows for the bit supplier?
open_questions.why_it_matters: One route (others: a changed recipe, split residuals, banks) to #1281's pooled rows or the window-free local rows; replica-local hosting on the frozen recipe is ruled out here.
open_questions.first_step: Compute windows on an interleaved bit timeline with owner_replica != replica and rerun the DP.
open_questions.blocked_by: An interleaved bit timeline (the selected T16 maps are complex-side) and a cross-replica DP; wopt.solve and the global_k.py anchor are specific to this per-replica schedule.

open_questions.question: Does another nine-stage stage recipe widen the capacity-7 windows?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The obstruction is recipe-specific; open #1487 enumerates recipes for width-8 hosting only.
open_questions.first_step: Generalise wopt's two-chain DP to arbitrary interval windows (or use a min-cost-flow bound), then apply it to #1487's hostable recipes.
open_questions.blocked_by: The generalised DP: wopt.solve asserts this recipe's chain structure.

open_questions.question: Do the window-respecting placements pass projector compatibility (#1307) for mixed-width slots?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Windows are necessary, not sufficient; slots that split q-perp lie outside #1307's completion-free argument.
open_questions.first_step: Rebuild the k = 1 placement with verify.build(1, plan, slots) and run #1307's projector check on the returned slot list.
